capability: # templates/capability-class.tsv — explicit GATE/AUTOFIX classification (HERD-424, audit P3.2
# docs/audits/2026-07-09-gating-hardening.md). A THIRD sibling manifest, keyed by capability NAME
# exactly as templates/capabilities.tsv column 1 (the SAME join key templates/conformance.tsv uses),
# so templates/capabilities.tsv stays byte-identical for its other consumers. PLAIN `herd conformance
# report` / `run` (bin/herd — no flag; the audit's own words were "make herd conformance report red on
# gate-class gaps") read this file to decide which capabilities MUST carry a real, EXISTING
# proof_kind=sim mapping in templates/conformance.tsv — NEVER an inference from capabilities.tsv's
# description prose (that was the audit's complaint: "today none-yet is allowed silently"). A capability
# absent from this file — the vast majority — carries NO requirement; the ratchet is a no-op for it and
# it keeps today's advisory mapped/rot/none-yet/unmapped behavior exactly as before this file existed.
# Columns:
#   capability   MUST match column 1 of templates/capabilities.tsv EXACTLY.
#   class        gate | autofix.
#                  gate    = decides WHETHER or WHEN a candidate proceeds toward merge: a pre-merge
#                            hold, a dispatch-order decision, a circuit breaker gating dispatch, the
#                            review gate itself, or fairness/queue ordering of a gates-passed PR.
#                  autofix = an AUTOMATIC repair action the watcher takes mid-pipeline on the
#                            candidate's behalf (a re-task bounce, a base-refresh heal).
#   note         free text — why this capability earned a class. Not read by any code path; the class
#                column alone drives the ratchet, so a note can never silently reclassify a capability.
# THE TEST: AGENTS.md's own "Sim-first for load-bearing changes" doctrine — "Any change to gate /
# merge / concurrency / limit / pane behavior must be proven with a simulation, not only unit asserts."
# A row here sits inside that doctrine's MERGE-DECISION or AUTO-REPAIR slice specifically (not every
# concurrency/pane capability the doctrine also covers — e.g. RESOLVER_PANE/HEALTH_PANE already carry
# real sim proof of their own but stay unclassified here: they are pane INFRA, not a merge decision or
# a repair action, so this ratchet does not require them to justify their sim on pain of a red report).
# INCREMENTAL BY DESIGN: this is the FIRST classified cohort (HERD-424), not an exhaustive one-shot
# re-audit of every capabilities.tsv row. Add a row whenever a NEW gate/autofix capability ships — that
# IS the ratchet: plain `herd conformance report` fails loudly the moment a classified capability has no
# honest sim proof, so a new gate/autofix ships with sim proof BY CONSTRUCTION instead of being
# discovered missing later. FAIL-SOFT is still absolute for a project that never creates this file at
# all — nothing is enforced against classification that was never opted into.
